anchor: The marathon official at the start line scans bib numbers against a sorted roster (unique index): a second runner in bib 1042 is yanked off the course before the gun — no two racers ever share a number mid-race.
example: ALTER TABLE users ADD CONSTRAINT uq_email UNIQUE (email); / second signup with the same email: / ERROR: duplicate key value violates uq_email
confusables: Primary key — a PK is UNIQUE plus NOT NULL and one per table; UNIQUE constraints can be many and usually admit NULLs.
alternates: No two identical snowflakes (snowflake collides with the schema name).
mnemonic: SEVEN normal forms to tame your tables

definition: A declarative boolean expression evaluated on every insert or update; rows failing the check are rejected by the engine itself.
anchor: The amusement-ride height stick bolted at the gate: 'you must be price >= 0 to ride'. The machine measures every row at the turnstile — no operator judgment, no exceptions, not even for staff (admin scripts).
example: ALTER TABLE products / ADD CONSTRAINT positive CHECK (price >= 0); / UPDATE products SET price=-5; -- check violation
confusables: Trigger — triggers run arbitrary code and can see other rows; CHECK is a simple per-row predicate the engine fully understands.
alternates: Bar bouncer with a rulebook (the bouncer already guards BCNF).
mnemonic: SEVEN normal forms to tame your tables

definition: ON DELETE rules decide the children's fate when a parent row dies: CASCADE deletes them too, SET NULL blanks the link, RESTRICT blocks the delete.
anchor: Demolition day at the parent building: CASCADE flattens every tenant apartment with it; SET NULL leaves tenants standing in the street with no address on file; RESTRICT — the crane refuses to swing while anyone still lives there.
example: user_id BIGINT REFERENCES users(id) / ON DELETE CASCADE / DELETE FROM users WHERE id=7; -- orders go too
confusables: Foreign key concept (702) — that is the reference itself; cascade actions are the enforced reaction when the referenced row disappears.
alternates: Falling dominoes (dominoes encode only CASCADE, not SET NULL or RESTRICT).
mnemonic: SEVEN normal forms to tame your tables

definition: Versioned, ordered scripts that change the database schema in lockstep with code; every environment replays the same numbered steps to the same state.
anchor: The database carries a passport: every schema change is a numbered stamp on the next page. A fresh database replays every stamp in order and arrives at today; a hand-edit without a stamp creates a state no one can reproduce.
example: migrations/0042_add_total_to_orders.sql / tools: Flyway, Alembic, Rails, Liquibase / applied once, recorded in a schema_version table
confusables: Serialized-format schema evolution (767) — that keeps encoded records readable across versions; migration rewrites live tables with DDL.
alternates: Software changelog (changelogs describe; migrations execute).
mnemonic: SEVEN normal forms to tame your tables

definition: Zero-downtime schema change: add the new shape (expand), dual-write and backfill, switch reads, then drop the old (contract); each step suits both versions.
anchor: Replacing a bridge without closing the road: build the new span alongside (expand), let traffic use both while repainting the lanes (dual-write, backfill), and demolish the old span only when the last car is off it (contract).
example: 1) ADD COLUMN full_name / 2) code writes both; backfill old rows / 3) switch reads; 4) DROP first_name, last_name
confusables: Blue-green deployment — swaps whole app environments; expand-contract evolves one shared database both versions must use.

definition: Instrument systems with logs, metrics, and traces so you can ask NEW questions about unknown failure modes without shipping code.
anchor: Flying at night, the cockpit's gauges, radar, and voice recorder let you investigate questions you never planned - versus a single 'ENGINE OK?' idiot light. Three windows into one flight.
example: logs: what happened; metrics: how much / traces: where in the request path / debug the 3 AM incident without a redeploy
confusables: Monitoring - monitoring watches KNOWN failure modes on preset dashboards; observability lets you explore unknown ones.
alternates: A glass-bottomed boat over an opaque ocean.
mnemonic: five NINES - 99.999%: the digit of never failing

definition: Emit logs as key-value events (JSON) with level, timestamp, and correlation IDs - machine-queryable, not prose strings.
anchor: The librarian swaps diary scrawl for index cards with labeled fields - user_id: 42, order: A7, ms: 340 - and suddenly a machine finds every card where ms > 1000 in seconds.
example: log.info('order_placed', order_id=417, ms=92) / query: level=error AND service=checkout / versus grep-ing 'Order 417 was placed OK!!'
confusables: Metrics - a log records each discrete event in rich detail; metrics pre-aggregate cheap numbers over time.
alternates: Barcodes replacing handwritten shelf notes.
mnemonic: five NINES - 99.999%: the digit of never failing

definition: Per service track Rate, Errors, Duration (RED); per resource track Utilization, Saturation, Errors (USE) - the core dashboards.
anchor: The nurse carries two clipboards: for each SERVICE she charts Rate, Errors, Duration; for each ORGAN-resource (CPU-heart, RAM-lungs) Utilization, Saturation, Errors. Vitals, not anecdotes.
example: RED: req/s, 5xx %, p99 ms per endpoint / USE: CPU 85%, run-queue depth 12, IO errors / dashboards start here, not from vibes
confusables: Logs - metrics are cheap pre-aggregated numbers for trends and alerts; logs carry per-event detail.
alternates: Two dashboards: one for waiters, one for the kitchen equipment.
mnemonic: five NINES - 99.999%: the digit of never failing

definition: Propagate a trace/correlation ID across every service a request touches, recording timed spans that reconstruct the full journey.
anchor: Drop a dyed relay baton (the trace ID) into the first runner's hand; every service stamps its split time on the same baton. Read it at the finish to see exactly which leg was slow.
example: traceparent header flows A -> B -> C / span: db.query 210 ms inside POST /checkout / answer: which hop added the extra 2 s
confusables: Profiling - a profile aggregates CPU across all work in one process; a trace follows ONE request across service boundaries.
alternates: A dye packet flushed through the whole plumbing system.
mnemonic: five NINES - 99.999%: the digit of never failing

definition: Page humans on user-visible impact - error rate, latency, SLO burn - not on causes like CPU; cause signals belong on dashboards.
anchor: Page the doctor when the patient cannot breathe (users see errors), not every time some enzyme twitches (CPU hits 80%). Cause-alerts cry wolf at 3 AM until nobody comes.
example: page: checkout error rate > 1% for 5 min / ticket, not page: disk 80% full / every page must be urgent, real, actionable
confusables: Cause-based alerts - invaluable for diagnosis AFTER the symptom page; paging on them breeds alert fatigue.
alternates: A smoke alarm, not a lit-match counter.
mnemonic: five NINES - 99.999%: the digit of never failing

definition: An SLI measures service health, an SLO sets its target, and the allowed shortfall - the error budget - prices how much risk to ship.
anchor: The 99.9% SLO mints a monthly jar of 43 unreliability minutes (the error budget); the team spends coins on risky launches while the jar clinks, and freezes features when it empties.
example: SLI: % of requests served under 300 ms / SLO: 99.9% monthly -> budget of 43 min / budget spent -> freeze features, fix reliability
confusables: SLA - the SLA is the external contract with penalties; SLOs are stricter internal targets that protect it.
alternates: A monthly allowance for breaking things.
mnemonic: five NINES - 99.999%: the digit of never failing

definition: Endpoints reporting liveness (process up - restart if not) and readiness (able to serve - else remove from rotation).
anchor: The load balancer knocks on each server's door every few seconds: 'You alive? Ready for guests?' Two silences and your name quietly leaves the rotation - no guest is ever sent to the dark room.
example: GET /healthz -> 200 (liveness) / GET /ready checks DB and dependencies / k8s: failing readiness pulls the pod from the LB
confusables: Liveness vs readiness - liveness failure restarts the pod; readiness failure only stops traffic to it.
alternates: A pulse check versus a fit-for-duty check.
mnemonic: five NINES - 99.999%: the digit of never failing

definition: On SIGTERM: stop accepting new work, finish or hand off in-flight requests, flush buffers, release connections, then exit.
anchor: On SIGTERM the bartender calls LAST ORDERS: door closed to newcomers, in-flight drinks finished and paid, tabs written down - then lights out. No glass is snatched mid-sip.
example: trap SIGTERM: server.stop_accepting() / drain in-flight (30s timeout), flush logs / k8s: readiness off -> SIGTERM -> SIGKILL after grace
confusables: Crash-only design - that engineers safe recovery from abrupt kills; graceful shutdown avoids dropping work at all.
alternates: A theater ushering out act by act instead of cutting the power.
mnemonic: five NINES - 99.999%: the digit of never failing

definition: A practiced structure for outages: clear roles - commander, comms, scribe - mitigate first, diagnose after, communicate on a cadence.
anchor: The fire alarm hands out hats, not blame: one incident commander decides, a scribe timestamps everything, the rest fight flames. Roll back and stop the bleeding FIRST; autopsy later.
example: sev1 declared; IC assigned within 5 min / mitigate first: roll back before root-causing / scribe's timeline feeds the postmortem
confusables: Postmortem - response happens DURING the fire; the postmortem is the learning exercise after it is out.
alternates: An ER trauma team: stabilize first, diagnose second.
mnemonic: five NINES - 99.999%: the digit of never failing

definition: After an incident, analyze how the SYSTEM let the failure happen - never who to punish - so people share truth and fixes compound.
anchor: The team gathers around the fallen server like surgeons around a teaching cadaver: they dissect the system's organs, never the intern's hands. Slot 999: five nines end not in punishment but in learning.
example: doc: timeline, impact, causes, action items / ask 'what made that mistake easy?' never 'who?' / actions get owners: add canary, drill rollback
confusables: Blame-free vs accountability-free - blameless targets system causes, yet every action item still gets a named owner and deadline.
alternates: A black-box flight recorder read aloud without a courtroom.
mnemonic: five NINES - 99.999%: the digit of never failing
